title: 4.5 Dilations

icans: I can find the scale factor of a dilation and tell whether it is an enlargement or a reduction.
I can dilate a figure in the coordinate plane.
I can use a negative scale factor.

vocab: a _________________ in which a figure is enlarged or reduced with respect to a fixed point, the center of dilation
the ratio of a length in the image to the ________________ length in the preimage
a ___________ with a scale factor greater than 1
a ___________ with a scale factor between 0 and 1

blocks.sec: Part 1 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Scale factor: k = (image length) ÷ (preimage length). If k > 1 the dilation is an _______________; if 0 < k < 1 it is a _______________.

blocks.stem:
Find the scale factor. Is it an enlargement or a reduction?
a.  CP = 6 and CP′ = 15
b.  CP = 12 and CP′ = 4
Dilate △ABC with A(2, 1), B(4, 1), C(2, 3) by a scale factor of 3, centered at the origin.

notes: Negative scale factor: the image is on the _______________ side of the center (a dilation combined with a 180° rotation).

blocks.stem: Dilate (1, −3) by a scale factor of −2, centered at the origin.
A preimage side is 10 and the matching image side is 4. Find the scale factor. Enlargement or reduction?

tickets.stem: Dilate (6, −9) by a scale factor of 1/3, centered at the origin.
A dilation has a scale factor of 3. Is it an enlargement or a reduction?
